q: Why are jobs in agriculture and AI growing?
options: Fewer people want to farm
Drones and AI are just temporary fads
Farming does not need technology
Population is increasing while farmland is decreasing, requiring new technology
explain: Growing population plus less farmland creates demand for technology solutions that increase agricultural productivity.

q: What can you do right now to prepare for a career in agricultural technology?
options: Wait until college
Only study soybeans
Focus entirely on computer science
Take STEM classes and gain agriculture experience
explain: You can start building valuable skills immediately through STEM classes and agriculture experience.

q: According to the workbook, what role can AI play as a leveler in agriculture?
options: It delivers scalable, farm-size-agnostic decision tools, making advanced analytics affordable across diverse production systems
It replaces the need for any human decision-making
It only benefits the largest farming operations
It has no measurable effect on farm profitability
explain: AI has the potential to make advanced analytics affordable and useful across farms of many different sizes, not just the largest operations.

q: Which of these is an example of an agriculture-focused college path?
options: Computer science
Mechanical engineering
Plant breeding
Data science
explain: Plant breeding is one of the agriculture-focused paths listed, alongside agronomy, weed science, and genetics.

q: Why might a data scientist working with genetic data benefit from a background in genetics?
options: Genetics knowledge has no relevance to data science
It's required to operate a drone
It helps them understand and correctly interpret the data they're analyzing
Genetics only matters for mechanical engineering
explain: Skills and knowledge in genetics are useful for a data scientist working with genetic data, since understanding the subject matter improves the quality of the analysis.
